about: Celestia is a modular blockchain network that lets developers launch their own blockchains and rollups while outsourcing data availability to a shared base layer. Its native token TIA trades on crypto exchanges and the network launched its mainnet in late 2023. Customers are crypto developers and protocols; revenue comes from network fees paid in the token. The foundation is registered in Liechtenstein, with a distributed team, and has raised roughly 157 million dollars from venture investors. It is a crypto-native brand with almost no mainstream consumer awareness, although crypto firms have sponsored sport before.
cb_desc: Celestia provides a modular blockchain network to deploy .

wiki.title: Celestia
wiki.text: Celestia is a real-time 3D astronomy software program that was created in 2001 by Chris Laurel. The program allows users to virtually travel through the universe and explore celestial objects that have been catalogued. Celestia also doubles as a planetarium, but the user is not restricted to the Earth's surface, like in other planetarium software such as Stellarium. Celestia can display objects of various scales using OpenGL.

about: Groundcover is a Tel Aviv cloud-native observability company whose platform uses eBPF technology to monitor applications, logs and infrastructure inside Kubernetes environments, with a bring-your-own-cloud pricing model. Customers are engineering and DevOps teams at software and technology companies, paying through subscriptions. It was founded around 2021 and has raised about 160 million dollars in venture funding, including a 2026 round. It is a private B2B developer tool with little public brand awareness outside the software engineering community.

wiki.title: Groundcover
wiki.text: Groundcover or ground cover is any plant that grows low over an area of ground, which protects the topsoil from erosion and drought. In a terrestrial ecosystem, the ground cover forms the layer of vegetation below the shrub layer known as the herbaceous layer, and provides habitats and concealments for terrestrial fauna. The most widespread ground covers are grasses of various types.

about: authID is a Denver-based identity authentication company offering biometric face-based verification and passwordless login for enterprises, banks and fintechs, including its Verified and Ceremony products. It earns software subscription and transaction fees. Formerly Ipsidy, it rebranded as authID in 2021 and trades on Nasdaq under AUID. Total funding is about 110 million dollars. It is a small B2B cybersecurity brand with little consumer awareness.

Brand Engagement Network is a Wilmington, Delaware headquartered AI company (listed on Nasdaq as BEN, via a SPAC) that offers conversational AI avatars and agents for businesses in sectors such as financial services, healthcare and retail. Customers are enterprises that pay software subscriptions. Total funding is about 75 million dollars. It is a small B2B technology brand with little public awareness.

DOOR is a St. Louis, Missouri technology company that Crunchbase describes as providing integrated hardware and software, tagged under apps and artificial intelligence. The listing shows about $342 million in total funding, with the most recent round dated in 2025, indicating substantial investor backing. The customer type and specific product are not clear from the available data, so it should be treated as an early-stage B2B technology business in the US Midwest. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Laiye is a Beijing artificial intelligence and automation company, founded in 2015 and previously known for robotic process automation (RPA) and intelligent document processing, now offering AI agents and enterprise workflow tools. It serves large Chinese enterprises in finance, telecoms and manufacturing, plus some international clients, and earns software licence and subscription fees. It has raised about $200 million from investors including Hillhouse and Sequoia China. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

about: BetterCloud is a New York software company, founded in 2011, that offers a SaaS operations platform helping IT teams automate onboarding, offboarding, security and management of employee access across applications such as Google Workspace, Slack and Microsoft 365. Customers are mid-sized and large organisations, paying subscription fees. It has raised about $187 million from investors including Warburg Pincus and Bessemer. B2B IT software brand with limited recognition outside the IT community.

wiki.title: BetterCloud
wiki.text: BetterCloud, an independent software vendor based in New York, NY and with engineering offices in Atlanta, GA, builds unified SaaS management software. A venture-backed startup, BetterCloud has raised $187 million in total funding, with the most recent round was led by Warburg Pincus with series F funding with $75 million raised to date. A previous round of funding was done in April 2018 which was led by Bain Capital Ventures. In December 2016, BetterCloud completed pivot from G Suite to general SaaS management. In March 2026, BetterCloud was acquired by CoreStack.

about: Lido is a decentralised liquid staking protocol, with its main product letting users stake Ethereum and other proof-of-stake assets to receive tradable staked tokens such as stETH, while earning staking rewards. Governed by Lido DAO and its LDO token, it holds a large share of all staked ETH, billions of dollars in assets. Contributors are distributed globally and Crunchbase lists a London base. It earns a fee on staking rewards and raised about $167 million. Well known in crypto, not among general consumers.

Syniverse is a Tampa, Florida telecommunications technology company, founded in 1987 (as GTE TSI), providing messaging, roaming, number portability, analytics and network services that connect mobile operators and enterprises. Customers include most of the world's carriers and large businesses, and it is owned by private equity investor Carlyle. It has raised about $780 million. B2B telecom infrastructure company with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Syniverse
wiki.text: Syniverse is an American communications technology company with a focus on 5G roaming, communications platform as a service (CPaaS), A2P Messaging, roaming clearing and settlement, IPX, fraud prevention, mobile identify and authentication solutions, IoT, Private Networks and other emerging technologies leveraged by global enterprises and telecommunication carriers.

about: Clari is a Sunnyvale, California revenue operations platform, founded in 2012, using AI to forecast sales, track deals and manage pipeline for revenue teams. Customers are mid-size and large companies such as Okta, Workday and Zoom, which pay subscription fees. It has raised about $500 million, including a 2022 round at a $2.6 billion valuation. B2B software brand known to sales leaders, not to consumers.

wiki.title: Clari
wiki.text: Clari is an opera semiseria in three acts by Fromental Halévy, to an Italian libretto by Pietro Giannone. It was first produced at the Théâtre-Italien in Paris on 19 December 1828.

about: Outreach is a Seattle-based sales engagement platform, founded in 2014, using AI to help sales teams automate emails, calls and meetings, forecast deals and manage pipeline. Customers are sales organisations who pay subscription fees. It has raised about $490 million and was valued at $4.4 billion in 2021. B2B software brand known to sales teams, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Outreach
wiki.what: Provision of services to populations who lack access
wiki.text: Outreach is the activity of providing services to any population that might not otherwise have access to those services. A key component of outreach is that the group providing it is not stationary, but mobile; in other words, it involves meeting someone in need of an outreach service at the location where they are. Compared with traditional service providers, outreach services are provided closer to where people may reside, efforts are very often voluntary, and have fewer, if any, enforceable obligations. about: Dialpad is a San Ramon, California cloud business communications company, founded in 2011, offering an AI-powered phone, video meetings, contact centre and messaging platform. Customers are companies of all sizes that pay subscriptions per user, with revenue of a few hundred million dollars. It has raised about $450 million and was valued at $2.2 billion. B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness.

Alpheya is a software company based in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, that delivers cloud-native, AI-enabled technology, apparently for wealth and asset management. Crunchbase shows funding of $300 million. It likely sells platform software to banks and wealth managers in the Gulf region. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Revenue from consumer subscriptions and employer or health-plan contracts, with guided meditation, sleep, therapy and coaching services and AI features. Tens of millions of downloads worldwide. Private, venture-funded. Highly recognizable consumer wellness brand.

Customers are mid-size and large enterprises, education and healthcare, paying subscription fees. Venture-funded, with about $300 million raised. B2B network infrastructure brand, known mainly to IT buyers.

wiki.title: Nile
wiki.text: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeast Africa which empties into the Mediterranean Sea. At 7,088 kilometers (4,404 mi) long, it is the longest river in the world, although the volume of water it carries is much smaller than other major rivers such as the Amazon or the Congo. The Nile has played a central role in the environmental, economic, and cultural history of Africa for millennia.

wiki.title: Nile (company)
wiki.text: Nile is a multinational technology company that delivers network and security infrastructure services for enterprises and government organizations. The company is based in San Jose, California, and operates primarily in North America, with a presence in twenty-five countries across Asia, Europe, and the Middle East.

about: Boston-based data security and access governance platform that lets enterprises find, secure and control sensitive data across cloud data platforms. Customers are large banks, government agencies and health organizations paying subscriptions. Founded in 2015, venture-funded with about $258 million. B2B security brand known to data and security teams.

wiki.text: Immuta Inc. is an American data security platform and software company. The company provides a cloud-native data governance platform to businesses, governmental agencies, and healthcare organizations.

about: Copenhagen-based cloud data protection company offering a SaaS backup and recovery platform for Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Azure and other cloud applications, with data stored in its own blockchain-verified vault. Sold to businesses and public bodies, often through partners, as a subscription. Founded in 2007 by Michael Hansen, with about $240 million in funding. B2B software brand, known in IT circles in Europe.

wiki.title: Vega
wiki.what: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra
wiki.text: Vega is the brightest star in the northern constellation of Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr. This star is relatively close to the Solar System, at only 25 light-years from the Sun, and one of the most luminous stars in the Sun's neighborhood, being intrinsically brighter than any star nearer to the Sun. It is the fifth-brightest star in the night sky, and the second-brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, after Arcturus.

wiki.title: Vega (company)
wiki.text: Vega is a brand of plant based nutritional products. The company was started in Burnaby by Charles Chang and Brendan Brazier in 2004. In 2015, Vega was sold to Denver-based giant Whitewave Foods for US$550 million.

Customers are major Korean manufacturers. Raised about $40 million. B2B software with little public awareness. Crunchbase shows total funding of $40,190,553 and a headquarters in Seoul, South Korea; check the input data for scale.

GreyOrange is a robotics and AI company that builds warehouse automation, including its Ranger robots and GreyMatter fulfilment software, and is based in Suwanee, Georgia, with major operations in India. Founded in 2012, it serves retailers, e-commerce and logistics firms worldwide. It has raised several hundred million dollars from investors including Tiger Global and Mithril. Privately held, B2B with low consumer awareness.
